prompt: An update is three atomic block writes in this order: W1 writes the new data block, W2 points the inode at it, W3 marks it used in the bitmap. A crash can happen after any prefix of the writes, and the disk keeps writes in order.

trace.label: How many different crash states (including none and all writes)?
Crash after W1 only. The disk is
choices: consistent (the new block is simply unreferenced)

trace.label: Crash after W1 and W2. The disk is
choices: inconsistent (the inode points at a block the bitmap calls free)

trace.label: Which order makes every crash state safe?
choices: any order, because writes are atomic

explain: Three writes have prefixes of length 0, 1, 2 and 3: four states. Pointing at a block that is not marked used risks it being handed to someone else, so the bitmap must be written before the pointer. A leaked (used but unreferenced) block is the harmless failure.
